html:
SMTO-SKL-0057 — SMTO doesn't know which Microsoft 365 account to use

GUID: b562b3e0-31fd-5724-8b02-18ca9804328f
Slug: microsoft365-account-ambiguous
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • You have more than one Microsoft 365 account connected to SMTO that could do this, and the request didn't say which one. SMTO won't guess, so nothing was done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO "list my connected Microsoft 365 accounts" to see the names and email addresses it can use. This shows which accounts SMTO is choosing between, so you can pick the right one.
  2. In your next message, type @ and pick the saved entry for the account you want, then repeat your request. Picking the account directly tells SMTO exactly which mailbox or calendar to use.
  3. Or name the account in plain words, for example "use my work account you@company.com". SMTO can match the email address to one of your connected accounts.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the request and its reply names the account you picked.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste passwords or sign-in codes into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 account selection found more than one connected account eligible for the operation and no explicit or accepted account was given.

What this means

  • Account selection finds multiple eligible Microsoft profiles without one explicit or accepted unique identity. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Account selection finds multiple eligible Microsoft profiles without one explicit or accepted unique identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe account candidates and the accepted task binding.

How to fix it

  • Pass an explicit account_ref chosen from the accounts listed in the error details (or from microsoft365.accounts), or bind the intended Microsoft 365 Account parameter in the conversation; MicrosoftProfiles.account never selects by list order.
  • Choose an explicit account_ref from the safe account candidates; do not select an account by list order.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • One exact intended account_ref is selected without relying on storage order.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
